_comment: Ratchet floor for tests/test_setup_blocks_agree.py. This number may only go UP.
It is how many leading lines every fenced setup block agrees on -- measured, not
chosen. Lowering it records an intended divergence and needs the reason in the
commit message; raising it locks in a new shared line.
Written by the scaffolder, because the count depends on which toolchains this
tree was generated with: a python tree shares two leading lines and one that
also carries node shares three. A number baked into the template would be true
for one --language and red on arrival for the others.
It varies by time as well, which the number cannot. Arriving through
bin/skeletor-upgrade into a tree scaffolded long ago brings the floor for a
fresh scaffold, not for that tree -- which may already agree on more. The
failure then reads UPWARD and names the depth to raise it to; that is the
ratchet asking you to lock in a gain, not a defect. Read the enrolled block
list in the message first: a rise can also mean a document left the
Read the test's docstring before changing either way.
